title: Thresholds and expectation thresholds
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's proofs (2026) of four conjectures on thresholds and expectation thresholds. The second Kahn-Kalai conjecture: for every graph H with h >= 1 edges and at most n vertices, the threshold for G(n,p) to contain a copy of H is at most 2048 e^50 p_E(n,H)(1 + log_2 h). Talagrand's conjecture that integral and fractional expectation thresholds agree up to the factor 25 * 512^4. Talagrand's discrete convexity conjecture: if mu_p(D) >= 1 - 2^-75, the sets not covered by 2^75 members of D form a p-small family. The Ascoli-He-Park-Talagrand conjecture: every graph splits into a bounded number of pieces, each appearing at a constant multiple of the integral expectation threshold of the whole graph. Lessons 1-4 develop thresholds, copy counts, planted resampling, the tree covering theorem and the graph tree; lesson 5 proves a multiscale selector estimate and the rounding of fractional covers; lesson 6 uses biased Fourier weights, signed arrays and a covering lemma; lessons 7-8 prove embedding results for sparse pieces and assemble the decomposition.

checks.exact_checks: Python (scratch kk_checks.py and kk58_checks.py, outputs kk_checks.out and kk58_checks.out, 9 Oct 2026, 0 problems). Lessons 1-4: strict monotonicity of threshold functions and q <= q_f <= p_c (enumerated covers, linear programming); unions of product sets; copy counts and containment probabilities for 10 small graphs; the edge-subset form of p_E; p_E <= p_c from exact containment polynomials; the perfect-matching and isolated-vertex bounds; planting identity, posterior law and both parts of local resampling in generic form; the reduction lemma on 25 random disjoint trees with every W; conditional spread of graph extensions at empty and nonempty nodes; the cycle bound. Lesson 1 additions and lessons 5-8: q_f <= spread parameter on random families, the uniform perfect matching is e^2/n-spread (n <= 2000) and q_f(PM_n) <= e^2/n by linear programming (n = 4, 6, 8); maximal truncation exactly on 3000 random instances; the selector-move combinatorics exactly on 12 random families (minimal feasible moves, cover property, profiles, (3.6), (3.7), the counting bound and the likelihood identity); the entropy bound; the mean of Y_x for p down to 1e-40; q <= q_f <= C q on small families; biased Fourier identities, the global weight bound, the signed identity for 1-4 rows and Li's fractional cover exactly; grouping of unions; the covering-lemma construction with generic parameters; the couplings of Theorem 7.1 exactly; positive selectors; q lower bounds; Paley-Zygmund; compression exactly; amplification; layering on random graphs; star-forest constants; degeneracy splitting, the set Y and parity colourings on random graphs; all numerical constants; Exercises of all lessons.
checks.lint: kk_lint.py (scratch): headings, provenance line, balanced TeX delimiters, every sibling link resolved; one flagged label reference checked by hand (lesson 8 cites Lemma 1.1 of lesson 7).

Lean formalizations by OpenAI noted (families 175 and 176). The two-union fractional cover of Li is proved from the two-row signed identity. Hoeffding's inequality and Hall's theorem are cited from earlier programme lessons. Cited works: Kahn-Kalai, Frankston-Kahn-Narayanan-Park, Park-Pham (two papers), Mossel-Niles-Weed-Sun-Zadik (two papers), Dubroff-Kahn-Park, Tran, Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-Zhang, Talagrand (author's page), Pham, Bednorz-Martynek-Meller, Park, Li, Ascoli-He-Park-Talagrand; DeMarco-Kahn, Frankston-Kahn-Park, Fischer-Person, Friedgut, Ellis-Filmus-Friedgut, Lovett-Solomon-Zhang and Erdos-Renyi named for credit only.
